case_name: Tamecca Seril, a.k.a. Tamecca Tillard v. Commissioner

taxpayer.notes: Mother of two boys; elder son started at Morehouse College fall 2016. Under 59 1/2. Pro se. All dollar amounts rounded to nearest dollar. Filing status not stated.

adjustments: $747 New York State College Choice Tuition Program payment taxable
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Taxability of $15,000 (late rollover / waiver), 72(t) education exception, penalty
conceded: Respondent conceded taxability of the $747 New York 529 program payment, and any additional tax or penalty with respect to it

findings_of_fact.fact: 2016 IRA distributions $16,500 (Jan 8) and $38,000 (Jul 25), total $54,500; not age 59 1/2; $3,800 withheld from second
findings_of_fact.snippet: withdrawals totaling $54,500 from her individual retirement account (IRA): a distribution of $16,500 on

findings_of_fact.fact: 529 account withdrawals $15,099: $5,816 paid to petitioner, $9,283 directly to Morehouse
findings_of_fact.snippet: A third distribution, of $9,283, was made directly to Morehouse.

findings_of_fact.fact: Return reported $54,500 distributions, $39,500 taxable; Form 5329 reported $24,664 subject to 10% tax, additional tax $2,466
findings_of_fact.snippet: She reported $24,664 of her distributions as being subject to the 10% additional tax and reported additional tax of $2,466.

findings_of_fact.fact: CP2000 Sept 17, 2018 (response due Oct 17, 2018); NOD Dec 10, 2018; petition Mar 4, 2019
findings_of_fact.snippet: on December 10, 2018, the IRS issued her a notice of deficiency

findings_of_fact.fact: $15,000 redeposited to IRA April 27, 2020, nearly four years after final distribution; postal error unsubstantiated
findings_of_fact.snippet: nearly four years elapsed between petition- er's receipt of the final distribution and her redeposit of the $15,000 to her IRA.

findings_of_fact.fact: Payments to Morehouse in 2016: $9,283 from 529 plus $9,809 from bank = $19,092; $5,816 of the $9,809 was 529 money; $3,993 from IRA proceeds
findings_of_fact.snippet: This leaves $3,993 (viz., $9,809 - $5,816) as the amount that petitioner paid Morehouse using proceeds of her IRA withdrawals.

findings_of_fact.fact: Return figure $24,660 subject to 10% tax implies $29,840 claimed exempt
Court found petitioner credible and acting in good faith
findings_of_fact.snippet: we find that petitioner has demonstrated reasonable cause for her

issues.question: Is petitioner taxable on the full $54,500 of 2016 IRA distributions, including $15,000 she intended to roll over (waiver of 60-day requirement)?
issues.holding: Taxable on full $54,500; no rollover within 60 days and denial of waiver not against equity or good conscience
issues.computable_reason: 60-day window mechanically failed (redeposit ~4 years later); waiver aspect is discretionary but court found no qualifying factors

issues.question: To what extent are the distributions subject to the 10% §72(t) additional tax given the higher-education exception?
issues.holding: $3,993 used for qualified higher education expenses in 2016 is excepted; additional tax of $5,051 (10% x $50,507)
issues.computable_reason: Given found QHEE of $3,993 (from substantiated payments), tax = 10% x (54,500 - 3,993) mechanically

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty?
issues.holding: Not liable; reasonable cause and good faith (6751(b) not reached)

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: All $54,500 IRA distributions taxable; 72(t) additional tax $5,051 (on $50,507); no accuracy-related penalty; $747 529 item conceded by respondent

notes: Opinion inconsistency: amount reported as subject to 10% tax is $24,664 on p. 3 but $24,660 on pp. 10 and 13. Stipulated exhibits; findings of fact after trial.
